title: Panache
description:
I seem to have unfortunately missed this project, or I don't think I would have started my own project, but in any case, I have separately developed a formatter, linter, and LSP for Quarto/RMarkdown/pandoc: https://github.com/jolars/panache

It takes a different approach, and directly parses the syntax tree using rowan green-tree nodes instead of treesitter. 

LSP and linting are extremely early in development, but the parser and formatter are shaping up quite well.

It also has support for formatting code blocks by invooking exernal formatters (air, ruff, etc).

title: `` `$$` `` wreaks havoc on our parser
description:
our block parser does not take "in code span" into account when deciding to switch into display math mode. So `` `$$` `` puts the parser into display math mode and that completely changes the subsequent behavior.

It's not trivial to fix this, unfortunately.

We should check the prevalence of this construction in our corpus (#63); in quarto-web it appears a few times, because it's the kind of thing you'd expect to write in documents that teach you about Markdown. Otherwise, it might be rare.

(It's also possible that all problematic usages are fixable with an ugly insertion of a zero-width space in between the dollar signs. It's not a workaround that I'd be proud to explain to our users, but here we are.)

title: Simplified div syntax for definition lists?
description:
WRT #12 :

@hadley likes a simpler syntax:

```
* term1
  
  para with def1

  para with def2

* term2

  para with def1

  para with def 2
```

This is cleaner then what we have:

```
* term1
  * bulletlistitem with def1
  * bulletlistitem with def2
* term2
  * bulletlistitem with def1
  * bulletlistitem with def 2
```

The problem with the simplified definition is that Pandoc supports [more than one para per definition](https://pandoc.org/lua-filters.html#pandoc.DefinitionList). If we implement this, then, we will need to allow both syntaxes.

But we have reasons to not want multiple equivalent syntaxes. Multiple syntaxes increases the set of non-canonical documents. If the desugaring step is many-to-one, then the "resugaring step" needs to make a choice, which means that only one of the sugared notations is preserved under round tripping. That reduces the quality of the experience for collaborative writing.

title: Syntax proposal: `[f]{=w}`
description:
In our grammars, we handle raw specifiers `{=format}` and attribute specifiers `{#id .class}` fairly uniformly. We do this because it allows us to be efficient with the lookahead of the `{` token.

Effectively, the concrete tree we get out of `tree-sitter-qmd` allows raw specifiers anywhere that attribute specifiers are allowed.

This works well for code cells and code blocks, which we desugar into different Pandoc nodes in `quarto_markdown_pandoc`.

But what about a span with a raw specifier, like`[f]{=w}`? Two options:

1. Disallow it at the desugaring step
2. Give some semantics to it (that is, convert it into some Pandoc AST)

title: Better error messages with language specifiers in disallowed locations
description: We currently accept `{lang}` in place of a commonmark attribute specifier, generically. This is the only way I could get a one-lookahead parsing strategy. However, `[foo]{lang}` is not something that makes sense. We should offer a good error message here.
